On the not-approved flow, return to the earlier stage named in the description. Do not connect the decision gateway directly to the later stage, and do not omit the approval action task.

args.text: the description says a person accepts or denies an offer that another party sent, and the process then waits to receive an item from another party

trace.reason: Check whether the learned guidelines already cover modeling a person's accept or deny decision and receiving items from another party (P2, M9) before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: When the description states that items arrive from an outside source at times the process cannot predict, and that a participant then accepts or denies each arrived item: Model each arrival as its own intermediate catch event, labelled with the arrival itself (for example, the received item plus 'received'), placed on the sequence flow before the participant's decision. Model the accept-or-deny choice as a user task labelled with that decision action, not as a service task, and do not merge the arrival wait into the decision task. Branch on the outcome with an exclusive gateway labelled with a question.

When the description states that a later step proceeds only after a party approves or accepts something previously provided, so the approval decides whether the process continues: model the approval as an exclusive gateway with one outgoing flow per outcome (approved and not approved), not as an ordinary task that merely performs the approval

When the description says a team sends a request to outside actors and then takes in their returned items as work the team carries out, and no stated occurrence is one the process must wait for before it can continue: Model the taking-in of the returned items as a task placed on the sequence flow after the request task and before the next step that uses them. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event. Reserve an intermediate catch event for an occurrence the process must wait for before it can continue.

When the description mentions an outside party only as the recipient of a request the company sends, or as the target of a case the company hands over, and never describes that party's own actions as a process participant: Do not create a pool for that outside party and do not draw message flows to or from it. Model the sending of the request or the handover as a task in the company's own process, and model any awaited reply as an intermediate catch event or event-based gateway in that same process.

args.text: the description says another party must write a stated number of updates about the participant, with no stated waiting between them, so the updates are work to be taken in rather than arrivals the process waits for

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers counted updates from another party, to classify the relation of the counted-catch-event-loop guideline.

result.rule: Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

args.text: the description says a participant enters several separately described inputs, such as a topic and an amount, before a later step, and the generator merged them into one user task

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers separate user inputs before classifying the relation.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
